title: MTB ResiFiler
built_from: precomputed results of public ENA isolates; no live run

fastq.label: Illumina reads (FASTQ, paired or single)
fastq.note: Reads carry depth and allele fraction, so this chain can report sub-clonal variants and depth-confirmed deletions, and can fail a locus for low coverage instead of calling it susceptible.

fasta.label: Assembly or gene FASTA
fasta.note: An assembly has no read depth or allele fraction, so heteroresistance cannot be assessed and ResiFiler integrated calling's depth-confirmed deletion calls do not apply. Calling onward from here is not built yet.

tool_rationale.species: Mash screen estimates how much of each reference genome is contained in the sample without aligning it, so the MTBC check and the contamination flag take seconds and run before any expensive stage. It only recognises organisms in the panel, so it flags rather than identifies.
tool_rationale.qc: fastp reports quality, GC and adapter content in the same pass that performs the trimming, so the before and after statistics come from one tool and one set of definitions.
tool_rationale.trim: fastp detects adapters for paired-end reads from the read overlap, so the adapter sequence does not have to be known in advance, and a single pass keeps low-quality tails from reaching the aligner.
tool_rationale.align_reads: BWA-MEM is long established for short Illumina reads against a single small bacterial reference, and handles the short insertions and deletions that frameshift calls in pncA and katG depend on.
tool_rationale.align_assembly: minimap2 is built for long sequences and contigs. Aligning an assembly with a short-read aligner would split and mis-place the contigs, which is why the input type selects the aligner.
tool_rationale.markdup: PCR duplicates inflate apparent depth and allele fraction. samtools markdup marks them rather than deleting them, so the evidence is kept but duplicates are not counted as independent support.
tool_rationale.coverage: mosdepth gives per-region depth fast enough to report coverage at every resistance locus, which is what the rule "a locus below the depth threshold is reported Fail, never susceptible" needs.
tool_rationale.call_majority: Majority alleles are called by local re-assembly of each active region, which is what makes the indel calls reliable, under a haploid model: M. tuberculosis is haploid, so a diploid model would mis-handle the majority allele.
tool_rationale.call_lowfreq: Alleles present in a minority of reads are called separately, below the fraction at which a majority caller reports a site. This is what makes a mixed population (possible heteroresistance) visible instead of silently lost.
tool_rationale.call_largedel: Large deletions are called from split reads and read pairs and then confirmed by read depth. The WHO catalogue has explicit deletion and loss-of-function rules, most importantly for pncA, and a small-variant caller cannot trigger them because it does not call deletions of several kilobases.
tool_rationale.annotate: SnpEff annotates against the H37Rv CDS with the bacterial codon table and emits HGVS, which is the naming the WHO catalogue uses. The emitted positions are checked against the catalogue's own genomic coordinates before any lookup.

statement: Work in progress, shown for the SC&IS Silver Jubilee Symposium. This pipeline is being built in stages and the benchmarked architecture described in our abstract is not integrated here. It is a re-implementation, NOT the benchmarked ResiFiler configuration: no accuracy is claimed and every threshold is a provisional placeholder.
